This package includes one executable, `mesa`. Actions are performed by entering `mesa` followed by various subcommands. A list of available subcommands can be displayed by entering mesa help Any individual subcommand is documented by typing `mesa help` followed by the name of the subcommand, for instance, mesa help new will give information about what the `new` command does. For detailed instructions, see the readme on the github page at https://github.com/wmwolf/mesa_cli","authors":"William Wolf"},{"documentation_uri":"https://www.rubydoc.info/gems/mesa_script/0.2.1","metadata":{},"homepage_uri":"https://billwolf.space/MesaScript/","funding_uri":null,"bug_tracker_uri":null,"project_uri":"https://rubygems.org/gems/mesa_script","version":"0.2.1","sha":"5ec31cfe6ce0ca631a37de384b1ed50b7a28062c26cf736e31262b86aee416f9","platform":"ruby","changelog_uri":null,"source_code_uri":null,"licenses":["MIT"],"gem_uri":"https://rubygems.org/gems/mesa_script-0.2.1.gem","downloads":24573,"mailing_list_uri":null,"name":"mesa_script","wiki_uri":null,"version_downloads":934,"info":"MesaScript - a DSL for making dynamic inlists for the MESA stellar evolution code.","authors":"William Wolf"},{"documentation_uri":"https://www.rubydoc.info/gems/mesa_reader/0.1.0","metadata":{},"homepage_uri":"https://wmwolf.github.io","funding_uri":null,"bug_tracker_uri":null,"project_uri":"https://rubygems.org/gems/mesa_reader","version":"0.1.0","sha":"852012f8285635b3600d4fc9c2f711a96f6583a8431a3606e429dad0e98e11b1","platform":"ruby","changelog_uri":null,"source_code_uri":null,"licenses":["MIT"],"gem_uri":"https://rubygems.org/gems/mesa_reader-0.1.0.gem","downloads":4041,"mailing_list_uri":null,"name":"mesa_reader","wiki_uri":null,"version_downloads":4041,"info":"    MesaReader is a ruby module that contains three classes, MesaData,
    MesaProfileIndex, and MesaLogDir. These classes are intended to read in
    three types of files or directories, MESA history/profile logs, MESA 
    profile indexes, and entire MESA LOGS directories, respectively. The
    resulting objects can then be maniuplated to return useful data in a ruby
    or tioga script.

    In addition to simple returning of data columns (the primary function of 
    the MesaData class), some basic searching features are built-in, allowing 
    you to search for profiles that correspond to something in the history, or
    for parts of history columns that depend on other history columns. All
    returned vectors have many built-in methods since they are DVectors from
    the DObjects module in Tioga, which is a requirement.

    For detailed instructions, see the readme on the github page at 

    https://github.com/wmwolf/MESA_Reader
","authors":"William Wolf"},{"documentation_uri":"https://www.rubydoc.info/gems/gltail/0.1.8","metadata":{},"homepage_uri":null,"funding_uri":null,"bug_tracker_uri":null,"project_uri":"https://rubygems.org/gems/gltail","version":"0.1.8","sha":"e1367dff790b1299290cc5f15ead68afc57973cfa7bc915d0766d027437a1955","platform":"ruby","changelog_uri":null,"source_code_uri":null,"licenses":null,"gem_uri":"https://rubygems.org/gems/gltail-0.1.8.gem","downloads":47047,"mailing_list_uri":null,"name":"gltail","wiki_uri":null,"version_downloads":8612,"info":"== FEATURES: * Real-Time OpenGL view * Multiple logfiles on multiple servers * Configurable layout * Multiple logfile parsers (Apache Combined, Rails, IIS, Postfix/spamd/clamd, Nginx, Squid, PostgreSQL, PureFTPD, MySQL, TShark, qmail/vmpop3d) * Custom events * Show rate, total or average * If you can 'tail' it, you can visualize it * Written in Ruby using net-ssh & libopengl-ruby * Free!  == RUNNING: gl_tail --help gl_tail --new gl_tail.yaml gl_tail  You can press 'f' while running to toggle the attempted frames per second. Or 'b' to change default blob type, and space to toggle bouncing.  == REQUIREMENTS: * rubygems    0.9.4 * ruby-opengl 0.40.1 * net-ssh     1.1.2 * opengl/ruby development packages (ruby1.8-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libglu1-mesa-dev libglut3-dev)","authors":"Erlend Simonsen"}]
